    {
      "startEvent": 843,
      "endEvent": 1308,
      "reason": "An edited duplicate begins partway through E843, replaying the opening at E0 and continuing through the earlier animal-ethics question around E464. This is a replay block rather than a new exchange or opening teaser. E843 also contains the end of Harris's original answer, so its attribution is U; E844 onward is O."
    }
  ],
  "candidates": [
    {
      "startEvent": 272,
      "endEvent": 274,
      "contextStartEvent": 255,
      "contextEndEvent": 279,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "you'll never understand it and no honest scientist claims that that you will",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "shame"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Prager asserts a permanent limit on understanding cosmic origins and links the contrary expectation to scientific dishonesty (E272-E274), without supporting that limit. This could protect his creator inference from future explanation, but he does not explicitly exclude future evidence. The preceding design argument supplies an ordinary, disputable rationale (E255-E265)."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 378,
      "endEvent": 383,
      "contextStartEvent": 352,
      "contextEndEvent": 397,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "you have to believe in something",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "no",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "fear",
        "identity"
      ],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "The maxim supplies the missing bridge from disbelief in God to obligatory faith in humanity, supposedly needed to avoid despair (E378-E383). Harris's cooperation argument concerns consequences of murder (E364-E371), not this psychological necessity. Prager states a personal conviction, but also applies it generally to his opponent; no merits-independent exclusion is explicit."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 430,
      "endEvent": 435,
      "contextStartEvent": 413,
      "contextEndEvent": 450,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "anything you raise I'll actually give you a scholarly answer to",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "none"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The unrestricted promise and suggestion that Harris reads without scholarship could insulate the text by preemptively discounting criticism (E430-E435). However, Prager actually offers distinctions about servitude and historical conditions, conceding that daughters could be servants (E435-E441). A promise to answer is not clearly a declaration that every objection must fail."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 591,
      "endEvent": 596,
      "contextStartEvent": 574,
      "contextEndEvent": 620,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "any rational conversation will ultimately lead you to believe",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "none"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Harris predicts convergence if conversation continues long enough (E591-E596), potentially making persistent dissent evidence of insufficient discussion or rationality. He does not explicitly adopt that exclusion. His subsequent claim that scriptural trust also depends on human thoughts supplies a reason for reliance on humanity (E604-E615), though not for inevitable agreement."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 599,
      "endEvent": 603,
      "contextStartEvent": 583,
      "contextEndEvent": 620,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "those who don't believe in God have to believe in humanity",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "no",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "fear",
        "identity"
      ],
      "confidence": "high",
      "explanation": "After Harris's reply, Prager renews the compulsory-faith claim and despair alternative (E599-E603), treating Harris as conceding it. Harris instead distinguishes reliance on human-authored documents from faith in God (E604-E615). Neither exchange supplies a reason that nonbelief necessitates faith in humanity or despair; explicit protection against counterexamples is absent."
    }
  ],
  "contrasts": [
    {
      "startEvent": 732,
      "endEvent": 736,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "we'll see what the research leads us to",
      "explanation": "Prager explicitly leaves the benefits of the research open to future results. Whatever the merits of his subsequent comparative moral claim, this local response acknowledges uncertainty rather than guaranteeing an outcome."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 833,
      "endEvent": 842,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "I don't mean the universe in terms of stars and galaxies",
      "explanation": "Harris answers the challenge to feeling one with the universe by limiting the claim to conscious experience and the sense of self. This clarifies the earlier spiritual language rather than using it as proof of a cosmic connection."
    }
  ]
